acceptance.given: The Toolchain route registry and route validator are present for the supported Acceptance package routes.

oracle.expected: Route validation reports each supported Acceptance package route as present and callable, with successful evidence bound to the effective inspected content.
forbidden: A supported Acceptance package route is missing, removed, or uncallable.
Success is reported without binding evidence to the effective inspected content.
oracle.observable: A deterministic route-validation result enumerates the supported Acceptance routes and their effective-content binding.

acceptance.then: The supported Acceptance package routes remain available for use.
acceptance.when: The supported route set is used or evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the route validator against a fixture in which a supported Acceptance route is removed or made uncallable; require deterministic failure identifying the unavailable route.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Keep supported Acceptance package routes registered and callable, and require route validation to bind success evidence to the effective inspected content.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing supported VDD and Acceptance route names and callable behavior; rollback only the route-validation change.

slice_hint.state_transition: supported Acceptance routes available -> route validation confirms availability and effective-content binding
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All supported Acceptance routes are enumerated as present and callable, and no success result is emitted without effective inspected-content binding.

acceptance.given: Identity or execution facts supplied to the Toolchain semantic gate may be unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable.

oracle.expected: The semantic gate permits success only after identity and execution facts are independently verifiable; otherwise it returns a blocked or failed verdict with the unverifiable facts identified.
forbidden: A success outcome is reported while any identity or execution fact remains unverifiable.
Historical or assistant-only text is accepted as proof of verifiability.
oracle.observable: The semantic-gate verdict records fact verification status and blocks success when any required fact is unverifiable.

acceptance.then: Success remains blocked until identity and execution facts are verifiable.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the semantic gate with an identity or execution fact marked unknown, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable; require a non-success verdict and explicit fact-level reason.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Gate success on independently verifiable identity and execution facts and emit a blocked or failed verdict whenever any required fact is unverifiable.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing verdict schema and failure semantics; rollback only the additional verifiability gate.

slice_hint.state_transition: facts may be unverifiable -> verifier classifies each fact -> success allowed only when all required facts are verifiable
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: No success verdict exists unless every required identity and execution fact has verifiable evidence in the current evaluation.

acceptance.given: A target package is selected for inspection and its identity is not yet independently verified.

oracle.expected: Before effective inspection, an independent verification computes and records the target package identity from repository content and confirms the selected package matches it.
forbidden: Target package identity is treated as verified without an independent verification.
Inspection proceeds when computed identity does not match the selected target package.
oracle.observable: A verification artifact contains the independently computed target identity, selected target identity, comparison result, and invocation provenance.

acceptance.then: Target package identity has been independently verified.
acceptance.when: Before effective inspection of the target package.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute target identity verification against a substituted, wrong, escaping, or modified package; require deterministic rejection before effective inspection.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add an independent target-package identity computation and comparison before inspection; reject mismatches and unsafe target selections closed.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing target-selection interfaces while restoring prior fail-closed behavior on identity mismatch.

slice_hint.state_transition: selected target unverified -> independent identity computed and compared -> verified target or fail-closed rejection
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Effective inspection starts only after an independent identity match is recorded for the selected target package.

acceptance.given: Atomic Obligation command links are evaluated by the Toolchain conformance validator.

oracle.expected: Validation reports bidirectional Exact Cover: every Atomic Obligation maps to exactly its required commands and every included command maps back to exactly one covered Atomic Obligation, with no unmatched links.
forbidden: An Atomic Obligation lacks a required command link.
A command link is one-directional or unmatched.
Runtime success is used as proof of the structural partition constraint.
oracle.observable: The conformance report contains reciprocal obligation-to-command and command-to-obligation sets with equal cardinality and zero orphan nodes.

acceptance.then: Every Atomic Obligation has complete, reciprocal, exact command coverage.
acceptance.when: Whenever Atomic Obligation coverage is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the conformance validator on a coverage graph with a missing, duplicate, one-way, or orphan command edge; require deterministic structural validation failure.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate reciprocal Exact Cover between Atomic Obligations and commands, rejecting missing, duplicate, one-way, and orphan command links with a structural report.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing conformance input and report schemas; rollback only reciprocal command-coverage checks.

slice_hint.state_transition: command coverage relation unevaluated -> bidirectional Exact Cover evaluated -> pass with zero orphans or structural failure
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Conformance evaluation proves exact reciprocal command coverage for every Atomic Obligation and reports no orphan command nodes.
